title: Pakistan Tells Hospitals To Clear Bed Space For "Mass Casualty Incident" Ahead of Major Protest
author: Areeba Fatima
content:
Since you're a reader of Drop Site News, you probably are aware that we are,
more or less, the only Western news outlet that offers any serious
investigative coverage of Pakistan's authoritarian descent. We consider it
scandalous that a nuclear-armed country of 250 million people receives so
little attention. But we also have to be honest that we understand why that's
the case. Audiences aren't used to it, and only with regular reporting can we
get them there, creating a chicken-and-egg problem that can only be solved by
contributions from readers who do understand why it's so important. If you're
one of them, please consider chipping in few dollars as a vote of support for
more of this coverage.

media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4749f7f3-5a6f-4d9a-8aa4-077dab948e60_5500x3666.jpeg)Aleema
Khan, Uzma Khan, and Noreen Niazi, sisters of jailed former Prime Minister
Imran Khan, walk with supporters during a protest in Rawalpindi, Pakistan,
December 9, 2025. Photo: REUTERS/Salahuddin.

Police in Lahore detained former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan's three
sisters, Aleema Khan, Noureen Niazi, and Dr. Uzma Khan, along with their
children, on Sunday, as Khan's party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), prepares
to march on Islamabad on September 27 to demand his release.

Imran Khan's health has deteriorated significantly over the past few months
after more than three years in prison. His primary healthcare provider, Dr.
Faisal Sultan, has not been allowed to visit him for several weeks. In their
last meeting, Imran Khan told his sister Uzma Khan that he is subjected to
"absolute inhumane treatment." The Telegraph
[reported](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/08/21/imran-khan-being-
tortured-in-prison-says-sister/) her saying, "He told me to tell people
outside that they are being unjust to me, they don't listen to me, these are
not humans."

In all, eight members of his family were detained within 24 hours. The
children were released after a few hours of detention, Aleema Khan's son
Shershah Khan told Drop Site, but Khan's sisters remain in custody.

Simultaneously, several elected leaders of PTI were also arrested, and party
offices were raided in a nationwide crackdown ahead of the September 27 march.

At the same time, Islamabad's hospitals were placed on emergency footing.
Documents obtained by Drop Site show that federal health authorities issued
instructions before the planned protest, directing hospitals to prepare for a
potential "humanitarian crisis" and "mass casualty incident" in Islamabad.

The measures have now started to affect the patients in Islamabad hospitals.
On Monday, patients scheduled for surgeries were told that their procedures
would be postponed, according to people familiar with the situation. The
surgical departments are to be reconfigured for a potential influx of
casualties. "All scheduled elective (planned) surgical procedures are
postponed indefinitely," the documents state.

All forms of leave for medical, nursing, paramedical, administrative, and
support staff have been suspended, while employees already on leave have been
recalled immediately. To do this, patients that hospitals consider to be
"stable," or recovering are being discharged from the hospitals.

The instructions to hospitals show that the government is yet again preparing
a brutal crackdown on protestors. In a similar protest in November 2024, the
Pakistani military killed dozens of PTI protestors using live rounds and
snipers on the gathered crowds in the middle of the night. A Drop Site
[investigation](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/leaked-information-reveals-
pakistan) from the time showed that the Pakistani military had planned the
crackdown on the protestors. The military later successfully covered up the
total number of casualties from the incident and
[arrested](https://www.ifj.org/media-centre/news/detail/article/pakistan-
journalist-arrested-on-false-terrorism-charges) journalists trying to
investigate.

Imran Khan has been in prison
[since](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/5/pakistans-khan-in-jail-
for-3-years-pti-amnesty-slam-solitary-confinement) August 2023 after a vote of
no confidence was used to overthrow his government. In these three years,
several human rights organizations have called his imprisonment a case of
arbitrary detention, and the military leadership of Pakistan has cracked down
on members of his party all over the world. In August, concerns about Khan's
health reached a crescendo when he was taken to PIMS (Pakistan Institute of
Medical Sciences). Earlier this year, he
[reportedly](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckgdr9vr50po) lost 85% vision
in his right eye. Khan's wife has also been facing multiple health issues in
prison, under solitary confinement similar to Khan, including the complete
loss of vision in one eye, according to her sister.

Aleema Khan's arrest was backed by a formal order by the deputy commissioner
of Lahore and obtained by Drop Site News, which authorized the detention of
Aleema Khan and her driver, Muhammad Ameer, for 30 days under Section 3 of the
Maintenance of Public Order (MPO). A similar order circulated on social media
alleging similar charges against Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan. The MPO has been
used repeatedly to subdue protests by detaining organizers and accusing them
of threatening public safety.

Hours after Aleema's arrest, her son Shershah Khan
[announced](https://x.com/KhanShershah/status/2101733825000935674) on social
media that police had surrounded the family's Lahore residence. In Lahore,
Aleema and Uzma Khan's houses share a wall. Sources close to the family who
requested anonymity for safety reasons confirmed that officers remained
stationed outside for several hours before the rest of the family was arrested
and driven to an undisclosed location in armored vehicles.

"We only found out through social media that they took her under MPO; we have
no information about where they have taken her," Noreen Niazi said in a [press
conference before she was arrested.
](https://x.com/PTIofficial/status/2101819911286735142?s=20)"They don't
realize September 27 will be a huge day; we are all a part of the movement for
Imran Khan's freedom."

Later that day, a member of the family told Drop Site News, they forcibly
entered Uzma Khan's home as well. "Uzma Khan has a heart condition; she was
sleeping when two hundred men entered her house and broke down her bedroom
door." Uzma Khan wears a hijab, but, the family reported, the police did not
allow her to cover herself while she was being detained. "These women are in
their late sixties and mid-seventies, but their bags were packed since they
knew something like this could happen before the 27th," he said.

Despite the arrests, the family insisted the march should continue as planned.
"They don't need a case. They don't need the facade of an order," said Imran
Khan's nephew. "The people of Pakistan should step out for their own freedom."

Sameer Khosa, a prominent lawyer of the Supreme Court, spoke to Drop Site
about the legal implications of the MPO. "In recent years, it has been used to
prevent protests and detain political opponents when there is no other ground
of arrest available," he said. "It is not surprising that it has been used in
this case in advance of a call to protest."

"Imran Khan's sisters have been outspoken in the past to bring attention to
his solitary confinement, deteriorating health, and deprivation of his
meetings with family members and lawyers," said Khosa. "This is clearly an
attempt to contain any galvanizing figures in advance of the September 27 long
march."

The general secretary of PTI and the head of their legal affairs, Salman Akram
Raja, told Drop Site, "There is this law, MPO, which has been challenged
several times as unconstitutional, but it has been struck down, but it has
been revived." He further added, "This is a pathetic attack on Imran Khan's
family; it is completely unacceptable, and similar attacks have been happening
all across Punjab. Pakistan has become a fascist state effectively, so
nobody's life, liberty is safe."

The sisters are being represented by lawyers Taimur Malik and Rana Mudassar,
who aim to file a habeas petition in the next few days. In a press conference
today, senior party leader Barrister Gohar Khan confirmed the long march will
go as planned.

"In the four years since our government was overthrown, we have not been
allowed a single long march," he said. "We have gone to the high courts 25
times and 19 times to the Supreme Court. We raised our voice in the parliament
and the senate, but it has fallen on deaf ears."

According to Gohar, 1,500 workers, five parliamentarians, and one minister
have been abducted just this week.

In a video posted on social media, the Chief Minister of Pakistan's Khyber
Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, Sohail Afridi, recorded a
[message](https://x.com/PTIofficial/status/2101804418966634779?s=20)
condemning the arrest of Khan's sisters. He said security forces have been
attacking party infrastructure all over the province and that they also tried
to abduct a provincial minister.

PTI leader Taimur Jhagra confirmed this to Drop Site. "Yesterday there was an
incident where a provincial minister was followed by masked men and people got
injured in the firing," he said. "Another KP MPA (Member of Provincial
Assembly) was picked up from his house in Islamabad."

Addressing Imran Khan's sisters' detention, Jhagra said, "It is, sadly, a
reflection of a Pakistan today with an illegitimate setup, where everything
from the constitution to the judiciary, the bureaucracy to the media, are all
controlled and able to flaunt the law as they want it."

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who is a trusted friend of Field Marshall Asim
Munir, has vowed the government "will not leave any loopholes" in its response
if the party proceeds with the long march. "Do not harm yourself and your
workers," he threatened.

_Aqeedat Chishty contributed reporting._
